+# Fixed-cutoff Gram limit
+
+## Abstract
+
+The actual fixed-cutoff Gram matrices converge to their diagonal face weights.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (The normalized actual Gram matrix).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Apollonian/CutoffGramLimit.normalizedGram`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Apollonian/CutoffGramLimit.normalizedGram` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Rad Sarar Anando (2026). *Second adjacency eigenvalue of Apollonian networks: is theta_2(G_m)/2^(m/2) -> sqrt(2)?*. URL: <https://mathoverflow.net/questions/516405>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For natural k,t, normalizedGram k t is 2^(-(k+t)) times B B^T on the fixed actual vertex set Vertex k, where B=cutoffBlock k t. Powers here have natural exponents before inversion. The matrix comes from the ordinary zero-one graph adjacency.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (The limiting face-weight diagonal).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Apollonian/CutoffGramLimit.limitingDiagonal`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Apollonian/CutoffGramLimit.limitingDiagonal` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Rad Sarar Anando (2026). *Second adjacency eigenvalue of Apollonian networks: is theta_2(G_m)/2^(m/2) -> sqrt(2)?*. URL: <https://mathoverflow.net/questions/516405>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For natural k, limitingDiagonal k has diagonal entry faceCount k u divided by 2^k at each actual old vertex u, and zero off the diagonal.
+
+**Theorem 1.3 (Convergence on the fixed old vertex set).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Apollonian/CutoffGramLimit.normalized_gram_tendsto`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Apollonian/CutoffGramLimit.normalized_gram_tendsto` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Rad Sarar Anando (2026). *Second adjacency eigenvalue of Apollonian networks: is theta_2(G_m)/2^(m/2) -> sqrt(2)?*. URL: <https://mathoverflow.net/questions/516405>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For each natural cutoff k, normalizedGram k t tends as t tends to infinity to limitingDiagonal k in the finite matrix topology, hence also for the Euclidean operator norm. The diagonal uses the exact doubling recurrence of incident inner faces and the exact degree increments. Every off-diagonal entry lies between zero and 2t/2^(k+t), which tends to zero. The cutoff is fixed before taking the stage limit. This statement alone does not identify the second ordered eigenvalue of the limiting diagonal.
+
+## References

+# Actual cutoff dilation spectrum
+
+## Abstract
+
+Ordered spectra of the actual old-to-late graph block.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (The actual cutoff dilation).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Apollonian/CutoffOrderedSpectrum.cutoffDilation`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Apollonian/CutoffOrderedSpectrum.cutoffDilation` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Rad Sarar Anando (2026). *Second adjacency eigenvalue of Apollonian networks: is theta_2(G_m)/2^(m/2) -> sqrt(2)?*. URL: <https://mathoverflow.net/questions/516405>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For natural k,t, the real matrix cutoffDilation k t acts on Vertex k plus LateVertex k t and has blocks [[0,B],[transpose B,0]], where B is the actual zero-one cutoff adjacency block. The two diagonal blocks are zero and the vertex types may have unequal cardinalities.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (The second decreasing dilation eigenvalue).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Apollonian/CutoffOrderedSpectrum.cutoffSecond`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Apollonian/CutoffOrderedSpectrum.cutoffSecond` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Rad Sarar Anando (2026). *Second adjacency eigenvalue of Apollonian networks: is theta_2(G_m)/2^(m/2) -> sqrt(2)?*. URL: <https://mathoverflow.net/questions/516405>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For natural k,t, cutoffSecond k t is index one in the decreasing real Hermitian spectrum of cutoffDilation k t, with algebraic multiplicity. The four persistent seed vertices ensure this index exists.
+
+**Theorem 1.3 (The actual positive second-spectrum bridge).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Apollonian/CutoffOrderedSpectrum.cutoff_second_eq_sqrt_gram`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Apollonian/CutoffOrderedSpectrum.cutoff_second_eq_sqrt_gram` (`✓ std3`). ∎

+*Source.* Repository-derived.

+*Commentary.*
+
+For every natural k,t, if the second decreasing eigenvalue of the actual Gram matrix B B^T on Vertex k is strictly positive, then cutoffSecond k t is its positive square root. No equality of the old and late block sizes is assumed. Characteristic-polynomial zero padding and real-to-complex embedding retain the ordered positive prefix, signs and algebraic multiplicities. +# Actual cutoff spectral bounds
+
+## Abstract
+
+Euclidean spectral remainder bounds for the actual finite inner-face Apollonian graphs.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (Row and column bounds control the Euclidean operator).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Apollonian/CutoffSpectralBounds.l2_opNorm_le_schur`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Apollonian/CutoffSpectralBounds.l2_opNorm_le_schur` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Citation.* Jue Xu and LeanPool contributors (2026). *Finite rectangular Schur operator bound*. URL: <https://github.com/LeanPool/lean-pool/blob/bbc67ff1e3ac4fc6a969daf42985a0d8f988d0b8/LeanPool/LowWeightPauliDynamics/SchurCore.lean>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every RCLike field K, finite row type I and finite column type J, with decidable equality on J, let A be an I by J matrix over K. If real R,C are nonnegative, every sum over j in J of the norm of A(i,j) is at most R, and every sum over i in I is at most C, then the Euclidean operator norm of A is at most sqrt(R*C). Empty row or column types are included. The norm is explicitly Matrix.Norms.L2Operator. Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz first bounds the squared action of each row, and summation uses the column bounds. The theorem is a minimal licensed port of Jue Xu's proof and is consumed by the actual Apollonian late adjacency estimate.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (The actual directed late matrix).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Apollonian/CutoffSpectralBounds.lateDirected`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Apollonian/CutoffSpectralBounds.lateDirected` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Rad Sarar Anando (2026). *Second adjacency eigenvalue of Apollonian networks: is theta_2(G_m)/2^(m/2) -> sqrt(2)?*. URL: <https://mathoverflow.net/questions/516405>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For all natural k,t, lateDirected k t is a real matrix on the actual LateVertex k t type. Its u,v entry is one exactly when the constructed graph has the edge u→v oriented from strictly younger to strictly older birth, and zero otherwise. The actual late ordinary adjacency is the sum of this matrix and its transpose.
+
+**Theorem 1.3 (The actual late adjacency operator bound).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Apollonian/CutoffSpectralBounds.late_adjacency_norm_le`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Apollonian/CutoffSpectralBounds.late_adjacency_norm_le` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Rad Sarar Anando (2026). *Second adjacency eigenvalue of Apollonian networks: is theta_2(G_m)/2^(m/2) -> sqrt(2)?*. URL: <https://mathoverflow.net/questions/516405>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every natural k,t, the Euclidean L2 operator norm of lateAdjacency k t is at most 2*sqrt(3*(3*2^(k+t-k-1))). The exponent uses natural subtraction. The outgoing row sums of the directed matrix are at most three, and its incoming column sums are at most 3*2^(k+t-k-1), by the proved constructor-derived orientation and degree laws. The Schur bound controls each direction and transposition preserves the L2 norm. Empty late sets are included. No degree or spectral estimate is assumed.
+
+**Theorem 1.4 (Uniform bound with the original normalization).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Apollonian/CutoffSpectralBounds.late_adjacency_normalized_le`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Apollonian/CutoffSpectralBounds.late_adjacency_normalized_le` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Rad Sarar Anando (2026). *Second adjacency eigenvalue of Apollonian networks: is theta_2(G_m)/2^(m/2) -> sqrt(2)?*. URL: <https://mathoverflow.net/questions/516405>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every natural cutoff k and natural t≥1, the L2 operator norm of lateAdjacency k t divided by the real power 2^((k+t)/2) is at most 3*sqrt(2)/2^(k/2). The exponents in both real powers use real division by two. The bound is uniform in the later stage t and includes odd stages. It concerns the late induced block of the actual graph, and does not itself establish the ordered second-eigenvalue limit.
+

+# Second eigenvalue of the inner-face Apollonian stages
+
+## Abstract
+
+The exact all-natural-stage second ordinary-adjacency eigenvalue limit.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (The original limit along every natural stage).**
+
+$$\lim_{n \to \infty, n \in \mathbb{N}} \frac{\operatorname{secondEigenvalue}(n)}{2^{n/2}} = \sqrt{2}$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Apollonian/SecondEigenvalueLimit.result` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Resolves.* `Problems/radsarar-anando-2026-apollonian-second-eigenvalue` (proved) by `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Apollonian/SecondEigenvalueLimit.result`.
+
+<!-- scribe-open-problem-resolution-v1 {"problem_slug":"radsarar-anando-2026-apollonian-second-eigenvalue","declaration_gid":"D5/S3/Combinatorics/Apollonian/SecondEigenvalueLimit.result","resolution_kind":"proved"} -->
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Rad Sarar Anando (2026). *Second adjacency eigenvalue of Apollonian networks: is theta_2(G_m)/2^(m/2) -> sqrt(2)?*. URL: <https://mathoverflow.net/questions/516405>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For the actual finite simple unweighted graph stages defined in InnerFaceStages, the second decreasing real eigenvalue of ordinary adjacency, counting characteristic-polynomial multiplicity, divided by the real power 2^((n:Real)/2), tends along all natural n to sqrt(2). Stage zero is the plane K4 with outer vertices a,b,c and centre o. Each successor inserts one vertex in every inner face, joins it to that face’s three corners, retains all old vertices and edges, and never subdivides the outer face. The theorem has no supplied degree, spectral, randomness or eventual-stage premise.
+
+The proof formalizes the accepted ordinary argument linked in the source note. At every fixed cutoff k, the limiting Gram diagonal has central weight three, outer-corner weight two, and all remaining weights at most two. Its second decreasing eigenvalue is therefore two, including multiplicity. The compiled Gram convergence and Hermitian perturbation bound give convergence of the actual normalized second Gram eigenvalue to two and its eventual strict positivity. The unequal rectangular dilation identity then gives the normalized cutoff second eigenvalue tending to sqrt(2).
+
+The actual cutoff equivalence transports the full ordinary adjacency spectrum without changing its order or multiplicity. The difference from the cutoff dilation is exactly the block diagonal formed from old adjacency and the actual late induced adjacency. Its Euclidean operator norm is at most the sum of their two norms. Real inclusion in the complex field preserves the ordered eigenvalues and the Hermitian operator norm, so the frozen complex perturbation theorem applies lawfully to the actual real matrices. The normalized late block is uniformly bounded by 3 sqrt(2)/2^(k/2), while the fixed old block tends to zero with the stage. First choosing k and then the later stage makes both errors and the cutoff spectral error small. This proves the limit on every sufficiently large natural stage, preserving odd stages through the original real-power normalization.
+
+This is an application and formal completion of the accepted ordinary proof. It makes no literature-priority claim and does not treat source-page answer counts as mathematical evidence. Statements about other leading eigenvalues, normalized adjacency, Laplacians, random subdivisions and subdivision of the outer face are outside the theorem.

+# Unequal block dilation spectra
+
+## Abstract
+
+Positive second eigenvalues of unequal Hermitian block dilations.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (The complex unequal-block identity).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/SpectralTopology/RectangularDilation.unequal_dilation_second`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/SpectralTopology/RectangularDilation.unequal_dilation_second` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Rad Sarar Anando (2026). *Second adjacency eigenvalue of Apollonian networks: is theta_2(G_m)/2^(m/2) -> sqrt(2)?*. URL: <https://mathoverflow.net/questions/516405>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For arbitrary finite types I and J with decidable equality, let B be a complex I by J matrix and let P=[[0,B],[B*,0]] be Hermitian. Suppose I has at least two elements and the second decreasing eigenvalue of BB* is strictly positive. The second decreasing real eigenvalue of P equals the positive square root of the second decreasing eigenvalue of BB*. Both lists count algebraic multiplicity. The two block sizes may differ or the second block may be empty; strict positivity rules out insufficient positive rank. Zero padding preserves the positive ordered prefix. A permutation identifies the square padded dilation with P plus a zero block; roots of characteristic polynomials retain signs and multiplicities.
+
+**Theorem 1.2 (Real inclusion preserves the ordered spectrum).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/SpectralTopology/RectangularDilation.eigenvalues_ofReal`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/SpectralTopology/RectangularDilation.eigenvalues_ofReal` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Rad Sarar Anando (2026). *Second adjacency eigenvalue of Apollonian networks: is theta_2(G_m)/2^(m/2) -> sqrt(2)?*. URL: <https://mathoverflow.net/questions/516405>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For any finite index type with decidable equality, a Hermitian real matrix and its entrywise inclusion in the complex field have identical decreasing real eigenvalue lists. The equality preserves characteristic-polynomial multiplicities and all indices.
+
+**Theorem 1.3 (The real unequal-block identity).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/SpectralTopology/RectangularDilation.unequal_real_dilation_second`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/SpectralTopology/RectangularDilation.unequal_real_dilation_second` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Rad Sarar Anando (2026). *Second adjacency eigenvalue of Apollonian networks: is theta_2(G_m)/2^(m/2) -> sqrt(2)?*. URL: <https://mathoverflow.net/questions/516405>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For arbitrary finite types I and J with decidable equality, let B be a real I by J matrix and let P=[[0,B],[transpose B,0]] be Hermitian. If I has at least two elements and the second decreasing eigenvalue of BB* is strictly positive, the second decreasing real eigenvalue of P equals its positive square root. For real matrices B*=transpose B. The proof embeds entries in the complex field, transports the full characteristic-root multiset and its decreasing order, and applies the complex unequal-block identity.

+# Finite Gaussian coefficient sewing
+
+## Abstract
+
+Full finite complex bilinear Gaussian coefficient sewing with the native trace-log normalization.
+
+The finite external and shared mode types may be empty. All coefficients are complex bilinear Gaussian coefficients, with no conjugation. The shared occupation weight is the product of coordinate factorials. External coefficients retain their ordinary coefficient normalization; no external factorial is inserted.
+
+This is classical Gaussian/Bargmann-Fock calculus. The actual Gaussian coefficient is extracted from quadratic(K)^(degree/2)/(degree/2)!, using the existing native polynomial definitions. A fixed external row is represented as a finite polynomial times the shared Gaussian. The proof uses the actual Gaussian annihilation equation and induction in external occupation degree. Its base is the existing principal-block polynomial projection. At every positive step the external multiplicity d_i+1 is divided out, external lowerings reduce degree, and a shared lowering is the original creation shift. The resulting polynomial is finite at every fixed external occupation, independently of the size of the external and mixed matrix blocks.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Actual finite polynomial insertion).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/TwistedGround/FiniteGaussianSewing.polynomialGaussian`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/TwistedGround/FiniteGaussianSewing.polynomialGaussian` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+A polynomial monomial with coefficient c and occupation alpha contributes c times created(alpha,gaussianCoefficient(A)). This is the ordinary coefficient convolution of that monomial with the actual Gaussian. The map is linear in the polynomial.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (Actual block coefficient row).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/TwistedGround/FiniteGaussianSewing.row`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/TwistedGround/FiniteGaussianSewing.row` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+At shared occupation n the row with external occupation d is gaussianCoefficient(K,d.sumElim(n)).
+
+**Theorem 1.3 (Finite polynomial bridge for arbitrary external blocks).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/TwistedGround/FiniteGaussianSewing.row_polynomial`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/TwistedGround/FiniteGaussianSewing.row_polynomial` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every symmetric matrix K on X plus H and every external occupation d, a finite shared polynomial p has polynomialGaussian(K_HH,p)=row(K,d). No norm hypothesis occurs in this algebraic identity. Repeated coordinates and empty types remain included.
+
+**Theorem 1.4 (Actual external row contraction converges absolutely).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/TwistedGround/FiniteGaussianSewing.row_pair_norm_summable`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/TwistedGround/FiniteGaussianSewing.row_pair_norm_summable` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For symmetric K on X plus H and L on Y plus H, the actual row contraction is absolutely convergent when only K_HH and L_HH are strict Euclidean contractions. The external and mixed blocks are arbitrary. The two finite polynomial witnesses are obtained from row_polynomial, rather than assumed as certificates.
+
+**Definition 1.5 (Actual two-sided Gaussian insertion moment).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/TwistedGround/FiniteGaussianSewing.bilinearMoment`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/TwistedGround/FiniteGaussianSewing.bilinearMoment` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+H(alpha,beta) is the original bilinear factorial pairing of created(alpha,c_A) with created(beta,c_B). Its recurrence contains the exact coordinate multiplicity beta_i and the lowered occupation beta-e_i, including the zero-coordinate case.
+
+**Theorem 1.6 (Ordered resolvent for actual insertion moments).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/TwistedGround/FiniteGaussianSewing.bilinearMoment_resolvent_step`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/TwistedGround/FiniteGaussianSewing.bilinearMoment_resolvent_step` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For symmetric strict shared contractions A and B, set U_i=H(alpha+e_i,beta), V_i=H(alpha,beta+e_i), u_i=beta_i H(alpha,beta-e_i), and v_i=alpha_i H(alpha-e_i,beta). Actual factorial adjointness and absolute summability give U=B V+u and V=A U+v. The theorem proves U=(I-B A)^(-1)(B v+u). The inverse is ordered, no commutativity is imposed, and no division by the vacuum scalar occurs.
+

+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/TwistedGround/FiniteGaussianSewing.covariance`

+/-- The continuous linear map on `EuclideanSpace` attached to a (possibly rectangular) matrix.

+/-- Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz for one row: if row `i` of `A` has absolute sum at most `R`, then
+`‖(A *ᵥ y) i‖ ^ 2 ≤ R * ∑ j, ‖A i j‖ * ‖y j‖ ^ 2`. This is the row step of the Schur test used

+private theorem schur_row_sq_le (A : Matrix ι κ 𝕜) (y : κ → 𝕜) (i : ι) (R : ℝ)

+  have habs : ‖(A *ᵥ y) i‖ ≤ ∑ j, ‖A i j‖ * ‖y j‖ := by
+    simpa only [Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct, norm_mul] using

+      (∑ j, ‖A i j‖) * ∑ j, ‖A i j‖ * ‖y j‖ ^ 2 := by
+    apply Finset.sum_sq_le_sum_mul_sum_of_sq_le_mul univ

+    · intro j _; exact norm_nonneg _
+    · intro j _; positivity
+    · intro j _; exact le_of_eq (by ring)
+  exact ((pow_le_pow_left₀ (norm_nonneg _) habs 2).trans hcs).trans
+    (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hrow (Finset.sum_nonneg fun j _ => by positivity))

+/-- Squared form of the finite Schur test used in `apd:thm:layer_inflow`: if every row of `A`

+`∑ i, ‖(A *ᵥ y) i‖ ^ 2 ≤ R * C * ∑ j, ‖y j‖ ^ 2`. -/
+private theorem schur_mulVec_sq_le (A : Matrix ι κ 𝕜) (y : κ → 𝕜) {R C : ℝ}
+    (hR : 0 ≤ R) (hrow : ∀ i, ∑ j, ‖A i j‖ ≤ R)
+    (hcol : ∀ j, ∑ i, ‖A i j‖ ≤ C) :

+      ∑ i, R * ∑ j, ‖A i j‖ * ‖y j‖ ^ 2 :=
+    Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => schur_row_sq_le A y i R (hrow i)
+  have h2 : (∑ i, R * ∑ j, ‖A i j‖ * ‖y j‖ ^ 2) =
+      R * ∑ j, (∑ i, ‖A i j‖) * ‖y j‖ ^ 2 := by
+    rw [← Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_comm]
+    congr 1
+    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ => by rw [Finset.sum_mul]
+  calc (∑ i, ‖(A *ᵥ y) i‖ ^ 2)
+      ≤ R * ∑ j, (∑ i, ‖A i j‖) * ‖y j‖ ^ 2 := h1.trans_eq h2
+    _ ≤ R * ∑ j, C * ‖y j‖ ^ 2 :=
+      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left
+        (Finset.sum_le_sum fun j _ =>
+          mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hcol j) (sq_nonneg _)) hR

+    (hcol : ∀ j, ∑ i, ‖A i j‖ ≤ C) : ‖A‖ ≤ Real.sqrt (R * C) := by

+  exact ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound _ (Real.sqrt_nonneg _)
+    (fun y => schur_clm_le A y hR hC hrow hcol)

+/-- An inner face at the indicated stage. Each child is indexed by its omitted corner. -/
+abbrev Face : ℕ → Type
+  | 0 => Fin 3
+  | n + 1 => Face n × Fin 3
+
+/-- Old vertices persist, and a distinct new vertex is inserted in each inner face. -/
+abbrev Vertex : ℕ → Type
+  | 0 => Fin 4
+  | n + 1 => Vertex n ⊕ Face n

+instance faceFintype : (n : ℕ) → Fintype (Face n)
+  | 0 => inferInstanceAs (Fintype (Fin 3))
+  | n + 1 => @instFintypeProd _ _ (faceFintype n) inferInstance
+
+instance faceDecidableEq : (n : ℕ) → DecidableEq (Face n)
+  | 0 => inferInstanceAs (DecidableEq (Fin 3))
+  | n + 1 => by
+    letI := faceDecidableEq n
+    exact inferInstanceAs (DecidableEq (Face n × Fin 3))
+
+instance vertexFintype : (n : ℕ) → Fintype (Vertex n)
+  | 0 => inferInstanceAs (Fintype (Fin 4))
+  | n + 1 => by
+    letI := vertexFintype n
+    exact inferInstanceAs (Fintype (Vertex n ⊕ Face n))
+
+instance vertexDecidableEq : (n : ℕ) → DecidableEq (Vertex n)
+  | 0 => inferInstanceAs (DecidableEq (Fin 4))
+  | n + 1 => by
+    letI := vertexDecidableEq n
+    exact inferInstanceAs (DecidableEq (Vertex n ⊕ Face n))
+
+/-- The three corners of every inner face. A child replaces its omitted corner by its centre. -/
+def corner : (n : ℕ) → Face n → Fin 3 → Vertex n
+  | 0, f, i => if i = 0 then 3 else if i = 1 then f.castSucc else (f + 1).castSucc
+  | n + 1, (f, i), j => if j = i then Sum.inr f else Sum.inl (corner n f j)

+private theorem corner_injective (n : ℕ) (f : Face n) : Function.Injective (corner n f) := by
+  induction n with
+  | zero => revert f; decide
+  | succ n ih =>
+    rcases f with ⟨f, i⟩
+    intro j k h
+    by_cases hj : j = i <;> by_cases hk : k = i
+    · exact hj.trans hk.symm
+    · simp [corner, hj, hk] at h
+    · simp [corner, hj, hk] at h
+    · exact ih f (by simpa [corner, hj, hk] using h)

+/-- Membership in the actual corner triple. -/
+def Incident (n : ℕ) (f : Face n) (v : Vertex n) : Prop := ∃ i, corner n f i = v
+
+instance incidentDecidable (n : ℕ) (f : Face n) (v : Vertex n) :
+    Decidable (Incident n f v) := inferInstanceAs (Decidable (∃ i, corner n f i = v))
+
+/-- Exact unweighted adjacency; no new edges join two old vertices or two new vertices. -/
+def adjacent : (n : ℕ) → Vertex n → Vertex n → Prop

+  | n + 1, Sum.inl u, Sum.inl v => adjacent n u v
+  | n + 1, Sum.inl u, Sum.inr f => Incident n f u
+  | n + 1, Sum.inr f, Sum.inl v => Incident n f v
+  | _ + 1, Sum.inr _, Sum.inr _ => False
+
+instance adjacentDecidable : (n : ℕ) → DecidableRel (adjacent n)
+  | 0 => inferInstanceAs (DecidableRel fun u v : Fin 4 => u ≠ v)
+  | n + 1 => fun u v => by
+    cases u <;> cases v <;> simp only [adjacent]

+/-- The finite simple graph obtained by simultaneous subdivision of inner faces only. -/

+  symm := ⟨by
+    induction n with
+    | zero => exact fun _ _ => Ne.symm
+    | succ n ih => intro u v; cases u <;> cases v <;> simp_all [adjacent]⟩

+    by_cases hi : i = k <;> by_cases hj : j = k

+    · simp only [corner, hi, hj, ↓reduceIte, adjacent]

+    · simp [Finsupp.tsub_apply, Finsupp.add_apply, Finsupp.single_apply, Ne.symm hji]
+  by_cases hz : α i = 0
+  · have hiff : α ≤ n + Finsupp.single i 1 ↔ α ≤ n := by
+      constructor
+      · intro h j
+        by_cases hji : j = i
+        · subst j
+          simp [hz]
+        · simpa [Finsupp.add_apply, Finsupp.single_apply, Ne.symm hji] using h j
+      · intro h
+        exact h.trans le_self_add
+    by_cases h : α ≤ n
+    · simp only [annihilate, created, h, hiff.mpr h, ite_true, hz,
+        Nat.cast_zero, zero_mul, zero_add, Finsupp.tsub_apply, tsub_zero, hshift h]
+    · simp [annihilate, created, h, hiff, hz]
+  · have hα : α - Finsupp.single i 1 + Finsupp.single i 1 = α :=
+      Finsupp.sub_add_single_one_cancel hz
+    by_cases h : α ≤ n
+    · have hplus : α ≤ n + Finsupp.single i 1 := h.trans le_self_add
+      have hminus : α - Finsupp.single i 1 ≤ n := tsub_le_self.trans h
+      have harg : n - (α - Finsupp.single i 1) = n - α + Finsupp.single i 1 := by
+        ext j
+        have hj := h j
+        by_cases hji : j = i
+        · subst j
+          simp only [Finsupp.tsub_apply, Finsupp.add_apply, Finsupp.single_eq_same]
+          omega
+        · simp [Finsupp.tsub_apply, Finsupp.add_apply, Finsupp.single_apply, Ne.symm hji]
+      simp only [annihilate, created, h, hplus, hminus, ite_true, harg,
+        hshift h, Finsupp.tsub_apply]
+      have hn : ((n i - α i : ℕ) : ℂ) + (α i : ℂ) = (n i : ℂ) := by
+        exact_mod_cast Nat.sub_add_cancel (h i)
+      linear_combination -f (n - α + Finsupp.single i 1) * hn
+    · by_cases hplus : α ≤ n + Finsupp.single i 1
+      · have hminus : α - Finsupp.single i 1 ≤ n := by
+          intro j
+          have hj := hplus j
+          by_cases hji : j = i
+          · subst j
+            simp only [Finsupp.tsub_apply, Finsupp.add_apply, Finsupp.single_eq_same] at *
+            omega
+          · simpa [Finsupp.tsub_apply, Finsupp.add_apply, Finsupp.single_apply, Ne.symm hji]
+              using hj
+        have heq : α i = n i + 1 := by
+          have hu := hplus i
+          simp only [Finsupp.add_apply, Finsupp.single_eq_same] at hu
+          by_contra hh
+          apply h
+          intro j
+          by_cases hji : j = i
+          · subst j
+            omega
+          · simpa [Finsupp.add_apply, Finsupp.single_apply, Ne.symm hji] using hplus j
+        have harg : n - (α - Finsupp.single i 1) = n + Finsupp.single i 1 - α := by
+          ext j
+          by_cases hji : j = i
+          · subst j
+            simp only [Finsupp.tsub_apply, Finsupp.add_apply, Finsupp.single_eq_same]
+            omega
+          · simp [Finsupp.tsub_apply, Finsupp.add_apply, Finsupp.single_apply, Ne.symm hji]
+        simp [annihilate, created, h, hplus, hminus, harg, heq]
+      · have hminus : ¬ α - Finsupp.single i 1 ≤ n := by
+          intro hh
+          apply hplus
+          rw [← hα]
+          exact add_le_add hh le_rfl
+        simp [annihilate, created, h, hplus, hminus]
+private theorem pairing_add_right (f g k : (H →₀ ℕ) → ℂ)
+    (hg : Summable (fun n : H →₀ ℕ => (weight n : ℂ) * f n * g n))
+    (hk : Summable (fun n : H →₀ ℕ => (weight n : ℂ) * f n * k n)) :
+    pairing f (fun n => g n + k n) = pairing f g + pairing f k := by
+  unfold pairing
+  simp only [mul_add]
+  exact hg.tsum_add hk
+/-- The actual two-sided creation moment, defined by the original bilinear
+factorial pairing and the original creation shifts. -/
+def bilinearMoment (A B : Matrix H H ℂ) (α β : H →₀ ℕ) : ℂ :=
+  pairing (created α (gaussianCoefficient A)) (created β (gaussianCoefficient B))
+/-- True creation/annihilation recurrence with both insertion monomials.
+The coordinate multiplicity is β_i, with zero-coordinate boundary terms
+included. Every infinite finite-sum exchange uses native summability. -/
+private theorem bilinearMoment_creation_step (A B : Matrix H H ℂ)
+    (hAsym : ∀ i j, A i j = A j i) (hBsym : ∀ i j, B i j = B j i)
+    (hA : ‖Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℂ) A‖ < 1)
+    (hB : ‖Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℂ) B‖ < 1)
+    (α β : H →₀ ℕ) (i : H) :
+    bilinearMoment A B (α + Finsupp.single i 1) β =
+      (β i : ℂ) * bilinearMoment A B α (β - Finsupp.single i 1) +
+        ∑ j, B i j * bilinearMoment A B α (β + Finsupp.single j 1) := by
+  let f := created α (gaussianCoefficient A)
+  let g := created (β - Finsupp.single i 1) (gaussianCoefficient B)
+  let t : H → (H →₀ ℕ) → ℂ := fun j n =>
+    B i j * created (β + Finsupp.single j 1) (gaussianCoefficient B) n
+  have hg : Summable (fun n : H →₀ ℕ => (weight n : ℂ) * f n * ((β i : ℂ) * g n)) := by
+    convert (created_pair_summable A B hAsym hBsym hA hB α
+      (β - Finsupp.single i 1)).mul_left (β i : ℂ) using 1
+    funext n
+    dsimp [f, g]
+    ring
+  have ht (j : H) : Summable (fun n : H →₀ ℕ => (weight n : ℂ) * f n * t j n) := by
+    convert (created_pair_summable A B hAsym hBsym hA hB α
+      (β + Finsupp.single j 1)).mul_left (B i j) using 1
+    funext n
+    dsimp [f, t]
+    ring
+  have hts : Summable (fun n : H →₀ ℕ => (weight n : ℂ) * f n * ∑ j, t j n) := by
+    simpa only [Finset.mul_sum] using summable_sum (s := Finset.univ) (fun j _ => ht j)
+  unfold bilinearMoment
+  rw [add_comm α, ← created_add, pairing_creation_annihilation,
+    annihilate_created_monomial, gaussian_annihilate B hBsym]
+  simp_rw [created_sum, created_const, created_add]
+  change pairing f (fun n => (β i : ℂ) * g n + ∑ j, t j n) = _
+  rw [pairing_add_right _ _ _ hg hts, pairing_const_right,
+    pairing_sum_right _ _ ht]
+  simp only [t, pairing_const_right]
+  rfl
+private theorem bilinearMoment_swap (A B : Matrix H H ℂ) (α β : H →₀ ℕ) :
+    bilinearMoment A B α β = bilinearMoment B A β α :=
+  pairing_comm _ _
+open scoped Matrix.Norms.L2Operator
+/-- The ordered resolvent equation for the actual two-sided factorial
+moments. This solves the creation/annihilation system without dividing by
+the vacuum scalar, and without assuming that A and B commute. -/
+theorem bilinearMoment_resolvent_step (A B : Matrix H H ℂ)
+    (hAsym : ∀ i j, A i j = A j i) (hBsym : ∀ i j, B i j = B j i)
+    (hA : ‖Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℂ) A‖ < 1)
+    (hB : ‖Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℂ) B‖ < 1)
+    (α β : H →₀ ℕ) :
+    (fun i => bilinearMoment A B (α + Finsupp.single i 1) β) =
+      Matrix.mulVec (1 - B * A)⁻¹ʳ
+        (Matrix.mulVec B (fun i => (α i : ℂ) *
+          bilinearMoment A B (α - Finsupp.single i 1) β) +
+          fun i => (β i : ℂ) * bilinearMoment A B α (β - Finsupp.single i 1)) := by
+  let U : H → ℂ := fun i => bilinearMoment A B (α + Finsupp.single i 1) β
+  let V : H → ℂ := fun i => bilinearMoment A B α (β + Finsupp.single i 1)
+  let u : H → ℂ := fun i => (β i : ℂ) * bilinearMoment A B α (β - Finsupp.single i 1)
+  let v : H → ℂ := fun i => (α i : ℂ) * bilinearMoment A B (α - Finsupp.single i 1) β
+  have hU : U = B.mulVec V + u := by
+    funext i
+    simpa only [U, V, u, Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct, Pi.add_apply, add_comm] using
+      bilinearMoment_creation_step A B hAsym hBsym hA hB α β i
+  have hV : V = A.mulVec U + v := by
+    funext i
+    have h := bilinearMoment_creation_step B A hBsym hAsym hB hA β α i
+    simp_rw [← bilinearMoment_swap A B] at h
+    simpa only [U, V, v, Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct, Pi.add_apply, add_comm] using h
+  have hrec : U = (B * A).mulVec U + (B.mulVec v + u) := by
+    rw [hV, Matrix.mulVec_add, Matrix.mulVec_mulVec] at hU
+    simpa only [add_assoc] using hU
+  have heq : (1 - B * A).mulVec U = B.mulVec v + u := by
+    rw [Matrix.sub_mulVec, Matrix.one_mulVec]
+    exact sub_eq_iff_eq_add.mpr (by simpa only [add_comm] using hrec)
+  have hBA : ‖B * A‖ < 1 := (norm_mul_le B A).trans_lt
+    ((mul_le_of_le_one_left (norm_nonneg A) hB.le).trans_lt hA)
+  have hu := isUnit_one_sub_of_norm_lt_one hBA
+  change U = Matrix.mulVec ((1 - B * A)⁻¹ʳ) (B.mulVec v + u)
+  calc
+    U = Matrix.mulVec ((1 - B * A)⁻¹ʳ) ((1 - B * A).mulVec U) := by
+      rw [Matrix.mulVec_mulVec, Ring.inverse_mul_cancel _ hu, Matrix.one_mulVec]
+    _ = _ := by rw [heq]
+private theorem resolvent_unit (A B : Matrix H H ℂ)
+    (hA : ‖Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℂ) A‖ < 1)
+    (hB : ‖Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℂ) B‖ < 1) : IsUnit (1 - B * A) := by
+  apply isUnit_one_sub_of_norm_lt_one
+  exact (norm_mul_le B A).trans_lt
+    ((mul_le_of_le_one_left (norm_nonneg A) hB.le).trans_lt hA)
+private theorem resolvent_push (A B : Matrix H H ℂ)
+    (hA : ‖Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℂ) A‖ < 1)
+    (hB : ‖Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℂ) B‖ < 1) :
+    (1 - B * A)⁻¹ʳ * B = B * (1 - A * B)⁻¹ʳ := by
+  have hleft := resolvent_unit A B hA hB
+  have hright := resolvent_unit B A hB hA
+  have hp : (1 - B * A) * B = B * (1 - A * B) := by noncomm_ring
+  calc
+    (1 - B * A)⁻¹ʳ * B =
+        (1 - B * A)⁻¹ʳ * (B * ((1 - A * B) * (1 - A * B)⁻¹ʳ)) := by
+      rw [Ring.mul_inverse_cancel _ hright, mul_one]
+    _ = (1 - B * A)⁻¹ʳ * (((1 - B * A) * B) * (1 - A * B)⁻¹ʳ) := by
+      rw [← mul_assoc B, ← hp]
+    _ = B * (1 - A * B)⁻¹ʳ := by
+      rw [← mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc, Ring.inverse_mul_cancel _ hleft, one_mul]
+private theorem resolvent_transpose (A B : Matrix H H ℂ)
+    (hAsym : ∀ i j, A i j = A j i) (hBsym : ∀ i j, B i j = B j i) :
+    ((1 - B * A)⁻¹ʳ).transpose = (1 - A * B)⁻¹ʳ := by
+  have hAt : A.transpose = A := by ext i j; exact hAsym j i
+  have hBt : B.transpose = B := by ext i j; exact hBsym j i
+  simp only [← Matrix.nonsing_inv_eq_ringInverse, Matrix.transpose_nonsing_inv,
+    Matrix.transpose_sub, Matrix.transpose_one, Matrix.transpose_mul, hAt, hBt]
+/-- The ordered joint insertion covariance. The lower cross block is the
+transpose of the upper cross block for symmetric A and B. -/
+def covariance (A B : Matrix H H ℂ) : Matrix (H ⊕ H) (H ⊕ H) ℂ :=
+  Matrix.fromBlocks ((1 - B * A)⁻¹ʳ * B) ((1 - B * A)⁻¹ʳ)
+    ((1 - A * B)⁻¹ʳ) ((1 - A * B)⁻¹ʳ * A)
+private theorem covariance_symm (A B : Matrix H H ℂ)
+    (hAsym : ∀ i j, A i j = A j i) (hBsym : ∀ i j, B i j = B j i)
+    (hA : ‖Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℂ) A‖ < 1)
+    (hB : ‖Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℂ) B‖ < 1) :
+    (covariance A B).IsSymm := by
+  have hAt : A.transpose = A := by ext i j; exact hAsym j i
+  have hBt : B.transpose = B := by ext i j; exact hBsym j i
+  unfold covariance Matrix.IsSymm
+  rw [Matrix.fromBlocks_transpose, Matrix.transpose_mul, Matrix.transpose_mul,
+    hAt, hBt, resolvent_transpose A B hAsym hBsym,
+    resolvent_transpose B A hBsym hAsym,
+    ← resolvent_push A B hA hB, ← resolvent_push B A hB hA]
+/-- The complete ordered Wick recurrence for the actual insertion moments,
+with symmetric joint covariance and both coordinate families. This is a
+recurrence for the actual infinite pairing, not an assumed Wick evaluation. -/
+theorem bilinearMoment_wick_recursion (A B : Matrix H H ℂ)
+    (hAsym : ∀ i j, A i j = A j i) (hBsym : ∀ i j, B i j = B j i)
+    (hA : ‖Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℂ) A‖ < 1)
+    (hB : ‖Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℂ) B‖ < 1) :
+    (∀ i j, covariance A B i j = covariance A B j i) ∧
+    (∀ (α β : H →₀ ℕ) (i : H),
+      bilinearMoment A B (α + Finsupp.single i 1) β =
+        (∑ j, covariance A B (.inl i) (.inl j) * (α j : ℂ) *
+          bilinearMoment A B (α - Finsupp.single j 1) β) +
+        ∑ j, covariance A B (.inl i) (.inr j) * (β j : ℂ) *
+          bilinearMoment A B α (β - Finsupp.single j 1)) ∧
+    (∀ (α β : H →₀ ℕ) (i : H),
+      bilinearMoment A B α (β + Finsupp.single i 1) =
+        (∑ j, covariance A B (.inr i) (.inl j) * (α j : ℂ) *
+          bilinearMoment A B (α - Finsupp.single j 1) β) +
+        ∑ j, covariance A B (.inr i) (.inr j) * (β j : ℂ) *
+          bilinearMoment A B α (β - Finsupp.single j 1)) := by
+  refine ⟨(fun i j => (covariance_symm A B hAsym hBsym hA hB).apply j i), ?_, ?_⟩
+  · intro α β i
+    have h := congrFun (bilinearMoment_resolvent_step A B hAsym hBsym hA hB α β) i
+    rw [Matrix.mulVec_add, Matrix.mulVec_mulVec] at h
+    simpa only [covariance, Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₁₁, Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₁₂,
+      Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct, Pi.add_apply, mul_assoc] using h
+  · intro α β i
+    have h := congrFun (bilinearMoment_resolvent_step B A hBsym hAsym hB hA β α) i
+    simp_rw [← bilinearMoment_swap A B] at h
+    rw [Matrix.mulVec_add, Matrix.mulVec_mulVec] at h
+    simpa only [covariance, Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₂₁, Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₂₂,
+      Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct, Pi.add_apply, mul_assoc, add_comm] using h
+private theorem polynomialGaussian_expansion (A : Matrix H H ℂ)
+    (p : MvPolynomial H ℂ) :
+    polynomialGaussian A p = fun n =>
+      ∑ α ∈ p.support, p.coeff α * created α (gaussianCoefficient A) n := by
+  calc
+    polynomialGaussian A p =
+        polynomialGaussian A (∑ α ∈ p.support, monomial α (p.coeff α)) :=
+      congrArg (polynomialGaussian A) p.as_sum
+    _ = _ := by
+      simp only [map_sum, polynomialGaussian_monomial]
+      funext n
+      simp only [Finset.sum_apply, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
+private theorem pairing_finset_right {T : Type*} (s : Finset T)
+    (f : (H →₀ ℕ) → ℂ) (g : T → (H →₀ ℕ) → ℂ)
+    (hs : ∀ i ∈ s, Summable (fun n : H →₀ ℕ => (weight n : ℂ) * f n * g i n)) :
+    pairing f (fun n => ∑ i ∈ s, g i n) = ∑ i ∈ s, pairing f (g i) := by
+  unfold pairing
+  simp only [Finset.mul_sum]
+  exact Summable.tsum_finsetSum hs
+private theorem polynomial_pair_moments (A B : Matrix H H ℂ)
+    (hAsym : ∀ i j, A i j = A j i) (hBsym : ∀ i j, B i j = B j i)
+    (hA : ‖Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℂ) A‖ < 1)
+    (hB : ‖Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℂ) B‖ < 1)
+    (p q : MvPolynomial H ℂ) :
+    pairing (polynomialGaussian A p) (polynomialGaussian B q) =
+      ∑ α ∈ p.support, ∑ β ∈ q.support,
+        p.coeff α * q.coeff β * bilinearMoment A B α β := by
+  have hp (α : H →₀ ℕ) : Summable (fun n : H →₀ ℕ =>
+      (weight n : ℂ) * polynomialGaussian B q n *
+        (p.coeff α * created α (gaussianCoefficient A) n)) := by
+    simpa only [polynomialGaussian_monomial, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul] using
+      (polynomial_pair_norm_summable B A hBsym hAsym hB hA q
+        (monomial α (p.coeff α))).of_norm
+  have hq (α β : H →₀ ℕ) : Summable (fun n : H →₀ ℕ =>
+      (weight n : ℂ) * created α (gaussianCoefficient A) n *
+        (q.coeff β * created β (gaussianCoefficient B) n)) := by
+    convert (created_pair_summable A B hAsym hBsym hA hB α β).mul_left
+      (q.coeff β) using 1
+    funext n
+    ring
+  rw [pairing_comm, polynomialGaussian_expansion A p,
+    pairing_finset_right _ _ _ (fun α _ => hp α)]
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro α hα
+  rw [pairing_const_right, pairing_comm, polynomialGaussian_expansion B q,
+    pairing_finset_right _ _ _ (fun β _ => hq α β)]
+  simp only [pairing_const_right, Finset.mul_sum, bilinearMoment]
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro β hβ
+  ring
+/-- The actual absolutely convergent external-row contraction is a finite
+sum of the true two-sided creation moments. Both polynomial witnesses are
+constructed from the original Gaussian coefficients; neither the vacuum
+normalization nor an effective-kernel identity is assumed. All coefficients
+are ordinary external coefficients and the shared weight is ∏ i, n_i!. -/
+theorem row_pair_moments {X : Type v} {Y : Type w}
+    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y]
+    (K : Matrix (X ⊕ H) (X ⊕ H) ℂ) (L : Matrix (Y ⊕ H) (Y ⊕ H) ℂ)
+    (hK : ∀ i j, K i j = K j i) (hL : ∀ i j, L i j = L j i)
+    (hA : ‖Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℂ) (fun i j => K (.inr i) (.inr j))‖ < 1)
+    (hB : ‖Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℂ) (fun i j => L (.inr i) (.inr j))‖ < 1)
+    (d : X →₀ ℕ) (e : Y →₀ ℕ) :
+    ∃ p q : MvPolynomial H ℂ,
+      polynomialGaussian (fun i j => K (.inr i) (.inr j)) p = row K d ∧
+      polynomialGaussian (fun i j => L (.inr i) (.inr j)) q = row L e ∧
+      Summable (fun n : H →₀ ℕ => ‖(weight n : ℂ) *
+        gaussianCoefficient K (d.sumElim n) * gaussianCoefficient L (e.sumElim n)‖) ∧
+      (∑' n : H →₀ ℕ, (weight n : ℂ) * gaussianCoefficient K (d.sumElim n) *
+        gaussianCoefficient L (e.sumElim n)) =
+        ∑ α ∈ p.support, ∑ β ∈ q.support, p.coeff α * q.coeff β *
+          bilinearMoment (fun i j => K (.inr i) (.inr j))
+            (fun i j => L (.inr i) (.inr j)) α β := by
+  obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := row_polynomial K hK d
+  obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := row_polynomial L hL e
+  refine ⟨p, q, hp, hq, row_pair_norm_summable K L hK hL hA hB d e, ?_⟩
+  simpa only [hp, hq, pairing, row] using polynomial_pair_moments _ _
+    (fun i j => hK (.inr i) (.inr j)) (fun i j => hL (.inr i) (.inr j)) hA hB p q
+private theorem sumElim_add_left {X : Type*} {Y : Type*} [DecidableEq X] [DecidableEq Y]
+    (d : X →₀ ℕ) (e : Y →₀ ℕ) (i : X) :
+    (d + Finsupp.single i 1).sumElim e = d.sumElim e + Finsupp.single (.inl i) 1 := by
+  ext (j | j) <;> simp [Finsupp.sumElim_apply, Finsupp.single_apply]
+private theorem sumElim_add_right {X : Type*} {Y : Type*} [DecidableEq X] [DecidableEq Y]
+    (d : X →₀ ℕ) (e : Y →₀ ℕ) (i : Y) :
+    d.sumElim (e + Finsupp.single i 1) = d.sumElim e + Finsupp.single (.inr i) 1 := by
+  ext (j | j) <;> simp [Finsupp.sumElim_apply, Finsupp.single_apply]
+private theorem sumElim_sub_left {X : Type*} {Y : Type*} [DecidableEq X] [DecidableEq Y]
+    (d : X →₀ ℕ) (e : Y →₀ ℕ) (i : X) :
+    (d - Finsupp.single i 1).sumElim e = d.sumElim e - Finsupp.single (.inl i) 1 := by
+  ext (j | j) <;> simp [Finsupp.sumElim_apply, Finsupp.tsub_apply, Finsupp.single_apply]
+private theorem sumElim_sub_right {X : Type*} {Y : Type*} [DecidableEq X] [DecidableEq Y]
+    (d : X →₀ ℕ) (e : Y →₀ ℕ) (i : Y) :
+    d.sumElim (e - Finsupp.single i 1) = d.sumElim e - Finsupp.single (.inr i) 1 := by
+  ext (j | j) <;> simp [Finsupp.sumElim_apply, Finsupp.tsub_apply, Finsupp.single_apply]
+/-- Identification of the actual factorial pairing with native Gaussian
+moments. The normalization is the native trace-log exponential. No inverse
+or nonvanishing premise for that scalar is used. -/
+theorem bilinearMoment_native (A B : Matrix H H ℂ)
+    (hAsym : ∀ i j, A i j = A j i) (hBsym : ∀ i j, B i j = B j i)
+    (hA : ‖Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℂ) A‖ < 1)
+    (hB : ‖Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℂ) B‖ < 1)
+    (α β : H →₀ ℕ) :
+    bilinearMoment A B α β =
+      Complex.exp ((1 / 2 : ℂ) *
+        ∑' n : ℕ, Matrix.trace ((A * B) ^ (n + 1)) / (n + 1 : ℂ)) *
+      NativeGaussianMoment.nativeMoment (covariance A B) (α.sumElim β) := by
+  obtain ⟨hC, hleft, hright⟩ := bilinearMoment_wick_recursion A B hAsym hBsym hA hB
+  let Z := Complex.exp ((1 / 2 : ℂ) *
+    ∑' n : ℕ, Matrix.trace ((A * B) ^ (n + 1)) / (n + 1 : ℂ))
+  have hzero : bilinearMoment A B 0 0 = Z := by
+    simpa only [bilinearMoment, created_zero, pairing] using
+      (vacuum_trace_log A B hAsym hBsym hA hB).2.2
+  have go : ∀ m (a b : H →₀ ℕ), a.degree + b.degree = m →
+      bilinearMoment A B a b =
+        Z * NativeGaussianMoment.nativeMoment (covariance A B) (a.sumElim b) := by
+    intro m
+    induction m using Nat.strong_induction_on with
+    | h m ih =>
+      intro a b hab
+      by_cases ha : a = 0
+      · subst a
+        by_cases hb : b = 0
+        · subst b
+          simpa [NativeGaussianMoment.nativeMoment, weight, gaussianCoefficient_zero] using hzero
+        obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := NativeGaussianMoment.occupation_nonzero b hb
+        let r := b - Finsupp.single i 1
+        have hr : r + Finsupp.single i 1 = b := Finsupp.sub_add_single_one_cancel hi
+        have hd : r.degree < m := by
+          have := NativeGaussianMoment.sub_single_degree b i hi
+          simp only [map_zero, zero_add] at hab
+          dsimp [r]; omega
+        rw [← hr, hright, sumElim_add_right,
+          NativeGaussianMoment.nativeMoment_step _ hC, Fintype.sum_sum_type,
+          mul_add, Finset.mul_sum, Finset.mul_sum]
+        congr 1
+        · apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+          intro j hj
+          simp
+        · apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+          intro j hj
+          have hjd : (r - Finsupp.single j 1).degree < m :=
+            (Finsupp.degree_mono (show r - Finsupp.single j 1 ≤ r from tsub_le_self)).trans_lt hd
+          rw [ih (r - Finsupp.single j 1).degree hjd 0
+            (r - Finsupp.single j 1) (by simp), sumElim_sub_right]
+          simp only [Finsupp.sumElim_inr]
+          ring
+      · obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := NativeGaussianMoment.occupation_nonzero a ha
+        let r := a - Finsupp.single i 1
+        have hr : r + Finsupp.single i 1 = a := Finsupp.sub_add_single_one_cancel hi
+        have hd : r.degree + b.degree < m := by
+          have := NativeGaussianMoment.sub_single_degree a i hi
+          dsimp [r]; omega
+        rw [← hr, hleft, sumElim_add_left,
+          NativeGaussianMoment.nativeMoment_step _ hC, Fintype.sum_sum_type,
+          mul_add, Finset.mul_sum, Finset.mul_sum]
+        congr 1
+        · apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+          intro j hj
+          have hjd : (r - Finsupp.single j 1).degree + b.degree < m :=
+            (Nat.add_le_add_right (Finsupp.degree_mono tsub_le_self) _).trans_lt hd
+          rw [ih _ hjd _ _ rfl, sumElim_sub_left]
+          simp only [Finsupp.sumElim_inl]
+          ring
+        · apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+          intro j hj
+          have hjd : r.degree + (b - Finsupp.single j 1).degree < m :=
+            (Nat.add_le_add_left (Finsupp.degree_mono tsub_le_self) _).trans_lt hd
+          rw [ih _ hjd _ _ rfl, sumElim_sub_right]
+          simp only [Finsupp.sumElim_inr]
+          ring
+  exact go _ α β rfl
+section ExternalRecurrence
+variable {X : Type v} {Y : Type w}
+  [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y]
+private def rowLower (K : Matrix (X ⊕ H) (X ⊕ H) ℂ) (d : X →₀ ℕ) (i : X) :
+    (H →₀ ℕ) → ℂ := if d i = 0 then 0 else row K (d - Finsupp.single i 1)
+private def rowPair (K : Matrix (X ⊕ H) (X ⊕ H) ℂ)
+    (L : Matrix (Y ⊕ H) (Y ⊕ H) ℂ) (d : X →₀ ℕ) (e : Y →₀ ℕ) : ℂ :=
+  pairing (row K d) (row L e)
+private theorem rowPair_swap (K : Matrix (X ⊕ H) (X ⊕ H) ℂ)
+    (L : Matrix (Y ⊕ H) (Y ⊕ H) ℂ) (d : X →₀ ℕ) (e : Y →₀ ℕ) :
+    rowPair K L d e = rowPair L K e d := pairing_comm _ _
+private theorem pairing_rowLower (K : Matrix (X ⊕ H) (X ⊕ H) ℂ)
+    (L : Matrix (Y ⊕ H) (Y ⊕ H) ℂ) (d : X →₀ ℕ) (e : Y →₀ ℕ) (j : X) :
+    pairing (row L e) (rowLower K d j) =
+      if d j = 0 then 0 else rowPair K L (d - Finsupp.single j 1) e := by
+  by_cases h : d j = 0
+  · simp [rowLower, h, pairing]
+  · simp only [rowLower, h, ite_false, rowPair, pairing_comm (row L e)]
+private theorem row_annihilate (K : Matrix (X ⊕ H) (X ⊕ H) ℂ)
+    (hK : ∀ i j, K i j = K j i) (d : X →₀ ℕ) (i : H) :
+    annihilate i (row K d) = fun n =>
+      (∑ j, K (.inr i) (.inl j) * rowLower K d j n) +
+        ∑ j, K (.inr i) (.inr j) * created (Finsupp.single j 1) (row K d) n := by
+  funext n
+  have h := congrFun (gaussian_annihilate K hK (.inr i)) (d.sumElim n)
+  simpa only [annihilate, row, Finsupp.sumElim_inr, ← sumElim_add_right,
+    Fintype.sum_sum_type, created_single, Finsupp.sumElim_inl,
+    ← sumElim_sub_left, ← sumElim_sub_right, rowLower, ite_apply, row, Pi.zero_apply,
+    apply_ite] using h
+variable (K : Matrix (X ⊕ H) (X ⊕ H) ℂ) (L : Matrix (Y ⊕ H) (Y ⊕ H) ℂ)
+  (hK : ∀ i j, K i j = K j i) (hL : ∀ i j, L i j = L j i)
+  (hA : ‖Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℂ) (fun i j => K (.inr i) (.inr j))‖ < 1)
+  (hB : ‖Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℂ) (fun i j => L (.inr i) (.inr j))‖ < 1)
+include hK hL hA hB
+private theorem row_pair_created_summable (d : X →₀ ℕ) (e : Y →₀ ℕ) (i : H) :
+    Summable (fun n : H →₀ ℕ => (weight n : ℂ) * row K d n *
+      created (Finsupp.single i 1) (row L e) n) := by
+  obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := row_polynomial K hK d
+  obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := row_polynomial L hL e
+  have hs := polynomial_pair_norm_summable
+    (fun i j : H => K (.inr i) (.inr j)) (fun i j : H => L (.inr i) (.inr j))
+    (fun i j => hK (.inr i) (.inr j)) (fun i j => hL (.inr i) (.inr j))
+    hA hB p (MvPolynomial.X i * q)
+  rw [polynomialGaussian_X_mul, hp, hq] at hs
+  exact hs.of_norm
+private theorem pairing_row_combination (d : X →₀ ℕ) (e : Y →₀ ℕ)
+    (a : X → ℂ) (b : H → ℂ) :
+    pairing (row L e) (fun n =>
+      (∑ j, a j * rowLower K d j n) +
+        ∑ j, b j * created (Finsupp.single j 1) (row K d) n) =
+      (∑ j, a j * pairing (row L e) (rowLower K d j)) +
+        ∑ j, b j * pairing (row L e) (created (Finsupp.single j 1) (row K d)) := by
+  have hs (j : X) : Summable (fun n : H →₀ ℕ =>
+      (weight n : ℂ) * row L e n * (a j * rowLower K d j n)) := by
+    by_cases h : d j = 0
+    · simp [rowLower, h]
+    · convert ((row_pair_norm_summable L K hL hK hB hA e
+        (d - Finsupp.single j 1)).of_norm.mul_left (a j)) using 1
+      funext n
+      simp only [rowLower, h, ite_false, row]
+      ring
+  have ht (j : H) : Summable (fun n : H →₀ ℕ =>
+      (weight n : ℂ) * row L e n *
+        (b j * created (Finsupp.single j 1) (row K d) n)) := by
+    convert (row_pair_created_summable L K hL hK hB hA e d j).mul_left (b j) using 1
+    funext n
+    ring
+  have hss := summable_sum (s := Finset.univ) (fun j _ => hs j)
+  have hts := summable_sum (s := Finset.univ) (fun j _ => ht j)
+  simp only [← Finset.mul_sum] at hss hts
+  rw [pairing_add_right _ _ _ hss hts,
+    pairing_finset_right _ _ _ (fun j _ => hs j),
+    pairing_finset_right _ _ _ (fun j _ => ht j)]
+  simp only [pairing_const_right]
+private theorem rowPair_external_step (d : X →₀ ℕ) (e : Y →₀ ℕ) (i : X) :
+    (d i + 1 : ℂ) * rowPair K L (d + Finsupp.single i 1) e =
+      (∑ j, K (.inl i) (.inl j) *
+        (if d j = 0 then 0 else rowPair K L (d - Finsupp.single j 1) e)) +
+      ∑ j, K (.inl i) (.inr j) *
+        pairing (created (Finsupp.single j 1) (row K d)) (row L e) := by
+  calc
+    _ = pairing (row L e) (fun n => (d i + 1 : ℂ) *
+        row K (d + Finsupp.single i 1) n) := by
+      rw [pairing_const_right, pairing_comm]
+      rfl
+    _ = _ := by
+      simp_rw [row_step K hK d i]
+      have hh := pairing_row_combination K L hK hL hA hB d e
+        (fun j => K (.inl i) (.inl j)) (fun j => K (.inl i) (.inr j))
+      simp_rw [pairing_rowLower] at hh
+      simpa only [rowLower, ite_apply, apply_ite, Pi.zero_apply,
+        pairing_comm (row L e)] using hh
+private theorem rowPair_internal_step (d : X →₀ ℕ) (e : Y →₀ ℕ) (i : H) :
+    pairing (created (Finsupp.single i 1) (row K d)) (row L e) =
+      (∑ j, L (.inr i) (.inl j) *
+        (if e j = 0 then 0 else rowPair K L d (e - Finsupp.single j 1))) +
+      ∑ j, L (.inr i) (.inr j) *
+        pairing (row K d) (created (Finsupp.single j 1) (row L e)) := by
+  rw [pairing_creation_annihilation, row_annihilate L hL]
+  have hh := pairing_row_combination L K hL hK hB hA e d
+    (fun j => L (.inr i) (.inl j)) (fun j => L (.inr i) (.inr j))
+  simpa only [pairing_rowLower, ← rowPair_swap K L] using hh
+private theorem rowPair_resolved_step (d : X →₀ ℕ) (e : Y →₀ ℕ) :
+    let A : Matrix H H ℂ := fun i j => K (.inr i) (.inr j)
+    let B : Matrix H H ℂ := fun i j => L (.inr i) (.inr j)
+    let P : Matrix X X ℂ := fun i j => K (.inl i) (.inl j)
+    let R : Matrix X H ℂ := fun i j => K (.inl i) (.inr j)
+    let Rt : Matrix H X ℂ := fun i j => K (.inr i) (.inl j)
+    let S : Matrix H Y ℂ := fun i j => L (.inr i) (.inl j)
+    let N : Matrix H H ℂ := (1 - B * A)⁻¹ʳ
+    (fun i => (d i + 1 : ℂ) * rowPair K L (d + Finsupp.single i 1) e) =
+      (P + (((R * N : Matrix X H ℂ) * B : Matrix X H ℂ) * Rt : Matrix X X ℂ)).mulVec
+        (fun j => if d j = 0 then 0 else rowPair K L (d - Finsupp.single j 1) e) +
+      ((R * N : Matrix X H ℂ) * S : Matrix X Y ℂ).mulVec
+        (fun j => if e j = 0 then 0 else rowPair K L d (e - Finsupp.single j 1)) := by
+  let A : Matrix H H ℂ := fun i j => K (.inr i) (.inr j)
+  let B : Matrix H H ℂ := fun i j => L (.inr i) (.inr j)
+  let P : Matrix X X ℂ := fun i j => K (.inl i) (.inl j)
+  let R : Matrix X H ℂ := fun i j => K (.inl i) (.inr j)
+  let Rt : Matrix H X ℂ := fun i j => K (.inr i) (.inl j)
+  let S : Matrix H Y ℂ := fun i j => L (.inr i) (.inl j)
+  let l : X → ℂ := fun j => if d j = 0 then 0 else rowPair K L (d - Finsupp.single j 1) e
+  let r : Y → ℂ := fun j => if e j = 0 then 0 else rowPair K L d (e - Finsupp.single j 1)
+  let U : H → ℂ := fun i => pairing (created (Finsupp.single i 1) (row K d)) (row L e)
+  let V : H → ℂ := fun i => pairing (row K d) (created (Finsupp.single i 1) (row L e))
+  have hU : U = B.mulVec V + S.mulVec r := by
+    funext i
+    simpa only [U, V, B, S, r, Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct, Pi.add_apply, add_comm] using
+      rowPair_internal_step K L hK hL hA hB d e i
+  have hV : V = A.mulVec U + Rt.mulVec l := by
+    funext i
+    have hh := rowPair_internal_step L K hL hK hB hA e d i
+    simp_rw [← rowPair_swap K L] at hh
+    simpa only [U, V, A, Rt, l, Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct, Pi.add_apply,
+      pairing_comm, add_comm] using hh
+  have heq : (1 - B * A).mulVec U = B.mulVec (Rt.mulVec l) + S.mulVec r := by
+    rw [hV, Matrix.mulVec_add, Matrix.mulVec_mulVec] at hU
+    rw [Matrix.sub_mulVec, Matrix.one_mulVec]
+    exact sub_eq_iff_eq_add.mpr (by simpa only [add_assoc, add_comm, add_left_comm] using hU)
+  have hu : U = Matrix.mulVec ((1 - B * A)⁻¹ʳ)
+      (B.mulVec (Rt.mulVec l) + S.mulVec r) := by
+    have hunit := resolvent_unit A B hA hB
+    rw [← heq, Matrix.mulVec_mulVec, Ring.inverse_mul_cancel _ hunit, Matrix.one_mulVec]
+  have hstep : (fun i => (d i + 1 : ℂ) * rowPair K L (d + Finsupp.single i 1) e) =
+      P.mulVec l + R.mulVec U := by
+    funext i
+    exact rowPair_external_step K L hK hL hA hB d e i
+  change _ = (P + R * (1 - B * A)⁻¹ʳ * B * Rt).mulVec l +
+    (R * (1 - B * A)⁻¹ʳ * S).mulVec r
+  rw [hstep, hu]
+  simp only [Matrix.add_mulVec, Matrix.mulVec_add, Matrix.mulVec_mulVec,
+    Matrix.mul_assoc, add_assoc]
+end ExternalRecurrence
+/-- The effective complex bilinear Gaussian kernel, with ordered inverses.
+The lower cross block is written explicitly in its ordered form. -/
+def effectiveKernel {X : Type v} {Y : Type w}
+    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y]
+    (P : Matrix X X ℂ) (Q : Matrix Y Y ℂ)
+    (A B : Matrix H H ℂ) (R : Matrix X H ℂ) (S : Matrix H Y ℂ) :
+    Matrix (X ⊕ Y) (X ⊕ Y) ℂ :=
+  Matrix.fromBlocks
+    (P + R * (1 - B * A)⁻¹ʳ * B * R.transpose)
+    (R * (1 - B * A)⁻¹ʳ * S)
+    (S.transpose * (1 - A * B)⁻¹ʳ * R.transpose)
+    (Q + S.transpose * (1 - A * B)⁻¹ʳ * A * S)
+private theorem effectiveKernel_symm {X : Type v} {Y : Type w}
+    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y]
+    (P : Matrix X X ℂ) (Q : Matrix Y Y ℂ)
+    (A B : Matrix H H ℂ) (R : Matrix X H ℂ) (S : Matrix H Y ℂ)
+    (hP : ∀ i j, P i j = P j i) (hQ : ∀ i j, Q i j = Q j i)
+    (hAsym : ∀ i j, A i j = A j i) (hBsym : ∀ i j, B i j = B j i)
+    (hA : ‖Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℂ) A‖ < 1)
+    (hB : ‖Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℂ) B‖ < 1) :
+    (effectiveKernel P Q A B R S).IsSymm := by
+  have hPt : P.transpose = P := by ext i j; exact hP j i
+  have hQt : Q.transpose = Q := by ext i j; exact hQ j i
+  have hAt : A.transpose = A := by ext i j; exact hAsym j i
+  have hBt : B.transpose = B := by ext i j; exact hBsym j i
+  have hNB : ((1 - B * A)⁻¹ʳ * B).transpose = (1 - B * A)⁻¹ʳ * B := by
+    rw [Matrix.transpose_mul, hBt, resolvent_transpose A B hAsym hBsym,
+      ← resolvent_push A B hA hB]
+  have hVA : ((1 - A * B)⁻¹ʳ * A).transpose = (1 - A * B)⁻¹ʳ * A := by
+    rw [Matrix.transpose_mul, hAt, resolvent_transpose B A hBsym hAsym,
+      ← resolvent_push B A hB hA]
+  unfold effectiveKernel Matrix.IsSymm
+  rw [Matrix.fromBlocks_transpose]
+  congr 1
+  · conv_lhs => rw [Matrix.mul_assoc R _ B]
+    rw [Matrix.transpose_add, Matrix.transpose_mul, Matrix.transpose_mul,
+      Matrix.transpose_transpose, hPt, hNB]
+    simp only [Matrix.mul_assoc]
+  · simp only [Matrix.transpose_mul, Matrix.transpose_transpose,
+      resolvent_transpose B A hBsym hAsym, Matrix.mul_assoc]
+  · simp only [Matrix.transpose_mul, Matrix.transpose_transpose,
+      resolvent_transpose A B hAsym hBsym, Matrix.mul_assoc]
+  · conv_lhs => rw [Matrix.mul_assoc S.transpose _ A]
+    rw [Matrix.transpose_add, Matrix.transpose_mul, Matrix.transpose_mul,
+      Matrix.transpose_transpose, hQt, hVA]
+    simp only [Matrix.mul_assoc]
+/-- Full finite complex Gaussian coefficient sewing. Only the shared blocks
+are strict contractions; the external and mixed blocks are arbitrary. The
+external coefficients are ordinary, and all finite types may be empty. -/
+theorem finite_sewing {X : Type v} {Y : Type w}
+    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y]
+    (P : Matrix X X ℂ) (Q : Matrix Y Y ℂ)
+    (A B : Matrix H H ℂ) (R : Matrix X H ℂ) (S : Matrix H Y ℂ)
+    (hP : ∀ i j, P i j = P j i) (hQ : ∀ i j, Q i j = Q j i)
+    (hAsym : ∀ i j, A i j = A j i) (hBsym : ∀ i j, B i j = B j i)
+    (hA : ‖Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℂ) A‖ < 1)
+    (hB : ‖Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℂ) B‖ < 1)
+    (d : X →₀ ℕ) (e : Y →₀ ℕ) :
+    Summable (fun n : H →₀ ℕ => ‖(weight n : ℂ) *
+      gaussianCoefficient (Matrix.fromBlocks P R R.transpose A) (d.sumElim n) *
+      gaussianCoefficient (Matrix.fromBlocks B S S.transpose Q) (n.sumElim e)‖) ∧
+    (∑' n : H →₀ ℕ, (weight n : ℂ) *
+      gaussianCoefficient (Matrix.fromBlocks P R R.transpose A) (d.sumElim n) *
+      gaussianCoefficient (Matrix.fromBlocks B S S.transpose Q) (n.sumElim e)) =
+      Complex.exp ((1 / 2 : ℂ) *
+        ∑' k : ℕ, Matrix.trace ((A * B) ^ (k + 1)) / (k + 1 : ℂ)) *
+      gaussianCoefficient (effectiveKernel P Q A B R S) (d.sumElim e) := by
+  let K := Matrix.fromBlocks P R R.transpose A
+  let L := Matrix.fromBlocks Q S.transpose S B
+  let K₂ := Matrix.fromBlocks B S S.transpose Q
+  let E := effectiveKernel P Q A B R S
+  let Z := Complex.exp ((1 / 2 : ℂ) *
+    ∑' k : ℕ, Matrix.trace ((A * B) ^ (k + 1)) / (k + 1 : ℂ))
+  have hK : ∀ i j, K i j = K j i := by
+    rintro (i | i) (j | j)
+    · exact hP i j
+    · rfl
+    · rfl
+    · exact hAsym i j
+  have hL : ∀ i j, L i j = L j i := by
+    rintro (i | i) (j | j)
+    · exact hQ i j
+    · rfl
+    · rfl
+    · exact hBsym i j
+  have hE : ∀ i j, E i j = E j i :=
+    fun i j => (effectiveKernel_symm P Q A B R S hP hQ hAsym hBsym hA hB).apply j i
+  have hswap (a : Y →₀ ℕ) (n : H →₀ ℕ) :
+      gaussianCoefficient K₂ (n.sumElim a) = row L a n := by
+    have hh := InfiniteGaussianFock.gaussianCoefficient_enlarge K₂ Sum.swap
+      (fun _ _ h => by simpa only [Sum.swap_swap] using congrArg Sum.swap h) (a.sumElim n)
+    rw [Finsupp.mapDomain_swap_sumElim] at hh
+    have hmat : (fun i j => K₂ (Sum.swap i) (Sum.swap j)) = L := by
+      ext (i | i) (j | j) <;> rfl
+    rw [hmat] at hh
+    exact hh
+  have h00 : rowPair K L 0 0 = Z := by
+    have hh := bilinearMoment_native A B hAsym hBsym hA hB 0 0
+    rw [rowPair, row_zero, row_zero]
+    simpa [bilinearMoment, created_zero, NativeGaussianMoment.nativeMoment, weight,
+      gaussianCoefficient_zero, K, L, Z] using hh
+  have hleft (a : X →₀ ℕ) (b : Y →₀ ℕ) (i : X) :
+      (a i + 1 : ℂ) * rowPair K L (a + Finsupp.single i 1) b =
+        (∑ j, E (.inl i) (.inl j) *
+          (if a j = 0 then 0 else rowPair K L (a - Finsupp.single j 1) b)) +
+        ∑ j, E (.inl i) (.inr j) *
+          (if b j = 0 then 0 else rowPair K L a (b - Finsupp.single j 1)) := by
+    have hh := congrFun (rowPair_resolved_step K L hK hL hA hB a b) i
+    simpa only [K, L, E, effectiveKernel, Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₁₁,
+      Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₁₂, Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₂₁, Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₂₂,

+
+Rad Sarar Anando, [MathOverflow question 516405](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/516405), revision 1,
+GUID `8C9D6CD5-E3A3-4B25-BDB6-FF5A9A3D3A2B`.

+are not additional premises or results attributed to the formal theorem.
+The quoted construction and question, and their adapted mathematical exposition,
+are attributed under [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/).
+The adaptations use explicit finite vertex and face indices and separate
+the graph construction from the proposed spectral limit.
+
+## Exact construction and question
+
+> Let $G_0=K_4$ with outer triangle $abc$ and central vertex $o$.
+> $G_m$ is obtained from $G_{m-1}$ by inserting a new vertex into every
+> inner triangular face, joined to its three corners. The outer face
+> $abc$ is never subdivided.
+
+The graph is finite, simple and unweighted. Its ordinary adjacency eigenvalues
+are listed in nonincreasing order, with multiplicity. The question is
+
+$$
+\lim_{m\to\infty}\frac{\theta_2(G_m)}{2^{m/2}}=\sqrt2.
+$$
+
+The source's numerical observations and preliminary spectral bounds are not
+premises of the graph construction or of the combinatorial laws.
+The larger question about other leading eigenvalues is outside this target.
+
+## Construction correspondence
+
+The seed indices $0,1,2,3$ denote $a,b,c,o$ respectively. The three initial
+inner faces have ordered corners $(o,a,b),(o,b,c),(o,c,a)$.
+At each step the vertex type is the disjoint sum of the old vertex type
+and the current inner-face type. A new vertex is adjacent exactly to the
+three distinct corners of its own parent face. Old adjacency is retained;
+two vertices born in the same step are not adjacent.
+
+For each parent face there are three child faces. Child $i$ replaces corner
+$i$ by the parent face's new centre, retaining the other two corners.
+The outer triangle is separately distinguished by its seed vertices and
+is absent from the subdivision index. No closed vertex-count formula is
+needed for the spectral index; four persistent seed vertices suffice.
+
+## Reused mathematics and evidence boundary
+
+The accepted ordinary proof in
+[issue #24905](https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing/issues/24905#issuecomment-6548069659)
+uses exact degrees, at most two inner faces through an edge, and orientation
+from newer to older endpoints. The corresponding all-stage spectral target
+is tracked by [issue #24989](https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing/issues/24989).
+`D5.S3.Combinatorics.Apollonian.SecondEigenvalueLimit.result` proves the exact
+`InnerFaceStages.limitClaim`. At fixed cutoff, the second limiting Gram weight
+is two: the central seed has weight three, the outer seeds have weight two,
+and all other weights are at most two. Gram convergence and the unequal-block
+dilation identity give the cutoff limit. The actual adjacency remainder is
+controlled by the fixed old block and the birth-oriented late block. Choosing
+the cutoff and then the stage proves the stated limit along all natural
+stages, with the original real-power normalization. This formalizes the accepted
+ordinary argument; it is not a separate claim to an original solution.
+
+The finite source and literature screen did not authenticate an exact competing
+deterministic second-eigenvalue limit. Its unread limits include the complete
+2005 and 2009 papers and independent retrieval of the 2010 paper. This is no
+claim of exhaustive literature coverage, priority, or worldwide openness.
+Random one-face subdivision, subdivision of all four faces of a spherical
+$K_4$, normalized adjacency, and Laplacian operators have different hypotheses.

+
+# Second adjacency eigenvalue of the inner-face Apollonian stages
+
+## Problem
+
+Rad Sarar Anando's MathOverflow question 516405, revision 1,
+GUID `8C9D6CD5-E3A3-4B25-BDB6-FF5A9A3D3A2B`, asks whether the second largest
+ordinary adjacency eigenvalue, counted with multiplicity, satisfies
+
+$$\lim_{m\to\infty}\theta_2(G_m)/2^{m/2}=\sqrt2.$$
+
+Here $G_0$ is plane $K_4$ with outer triangle $abc$ and centre $o$.
+Every step inserts one vertex in each inner triangular face and joins it
+exactly to the three corners; the outer triangle is never subdivided.
+The [source note](../Library/Eigenstructure/radsararanando2026apollonian.md)
+attributes the quotation and adapted exposition to the author under CC BY-SA 4.0.
+
+## Motivation
+
+The dominant old vertices have exponentially growing degree, while their
+common late neighbours grow only linearly. A fixed old cutoff exposes this
+separation through the Gram matrix of the old-to-late adjacency block.
+
+## Gap
+
+The exact all-stage spectral limit is **Proved** by
+`D5.S3.Combinatorics.Apollonian.SecondEigenvalueLimit.result : InnerFaceStages.limitClaim`.
+It quantifies along every natural stage, including odd stages, without an
+additional degree or spectral hypothesis. This is the formal completion of
+the accepted ordinary proof attributed in the source note, rather than a
+claim to a new ordinary solution or worldwide priority.
+The forward preregistration is
+[issue #24989, comment 6550398124](https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing/issues/24989#issuecomment-6550398124).
+It retains unit 24989, cutoff `2026-11-01T11:00:00Z` and `predictions: []`;
+the earlier unit 24905 settlement is unchanged.
+
+## Route
+
+Fix $k$ and partition stage $m>k$ into $H=V(G_k)$ and later vertices $L$.
+The old-to-late block $B$ has Gram diagonal
+$\deg_{G_m}(v)-\deg_{G_k}(v)$ and off-diagonal entries at most $2(m-k)$.
+An inner vertex born at $j$ has degree $3\,2^{m-j}$; the centre has degree
+$3\,2^m$ and each outer seed vertex has degree $2^{m+1}+1$.
+Thus $2^{-m}BB^\top$ converges on fixed $H$ to a diagonal matrix whose second
+largest entry is $2$.
+

+## 26. 无预设内积的最小锐效应与三种范数
+
+**定义 26.1（操作载体、帧与两条原则）。** Let $A$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional real vector space, $A_+$ a closed, pointed, generating convex cone, and $u\in A^\vee$ strictly positive on $A_+\setminus\{0\}$. The dual cone is $A_+^\vee=\{f:f(A_+)\ge0\}$, and inequalities between functionals use this cone. States form $\Omega=\{x\in A_+:u(x)=1\}$; pure states are its extreme points. All effects in $[0,u]\subset A^\vee$ are admitted, each defining a binary cut $(f,u-f)$. A nonempty ordered frame $(\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_r)$ consists of pure states and effects $f_i$ with $\sum_i f_i\le u$ and $f_i(\omega_j)=\delta_{ij}$. Its unused effect $u-\sum_i f_i$ is allowed.
+
+Principle S says that each pure $\omega$ has a least saturating effect $e_\omega$: $e_\omega(\omega)=1$, and $e_\omega\le f$ whenever $f\in[0,u]$ and $f(\omega)=1$. It also requires reciprocity $e_\omega(\sigma)=e_\sigma(\omega)$ for all pure $\omega,\sigma$. Principle Sp says that every $x\in A$ has a signed frame decomposition $x=\sum_i\lambda_i\omega_i$, $\lambda_i\in\mathbb R$. Neither principle mentions an inner product. Define
+
+$$
+\|x\|_B=\inf_{x=a-b,\ a,b\in A_+}\bigl(u(a)+u(b)\bigr),\qquad
+\|f\|_u=\inf\{t\ge0:-tu\le f\le tu\}.
+\tag{26.1}
+$$
+
+**定理 26.2（最小锐效应的线性化与可量化范数分离）。** Under Definition 26.1 and S and Sp, every frame satisfies
+
+$$
+e_{\omega_i}(\omega_j)=\delta_{ij},\qquad \sum_i e_{\omega_i}\le u.
+\tag{26.2}
+$$
+
+The assignment $\omega\mapsto e_\omega$ extends uniquely to a linear isomorphism $\Phi:A\to A^\vee$. The form $\beta(x,y)=\Phi(x)(y)$ is symmetric positive definite and
+
+$$
+A_+=\{x:\beta(x,y)\ge0\text{ for all }y\in A_+\}.
+\tag{26.3}
+$$
+
+For every signed frame decomposition, including frames not maximal,
+
+$$
+\|x\|_B=\sum_i|\lambda_i|,\qquad
+\|\Phi(x)\|_u=\max_i|\lambda_i|,\qquad
+\|x\|_\beta=\sqrt{\beta(x,x)}=\left(\sum_i\lambda_i^2\right)^{1/2}.
+\tag{26.4}
+$$
+
+These quantities are independent of the decomposition. If a two-element frame exists, the parallelogram sides $\|x+y\|^2+\|x-y\|^2$ and $2\|x\|^2+2\|y\|^2$, at $x=\omega_1,y=\omega_2$, are respectively $8,4$ for the base norm, $2,4$ for the pulled-back order-unit norm, and $4,4$ for the $\beta$ norm. The $\beta$ norm satisfies the parallelogram law for every pair of vectors.
+
+**证明。** Since $0\le e_{\omega_i}\le f_i$, all off-diagonal evaluations vanish and (26.2) follows, with diagonal value one. Sp makes pure states span $A$. If $\sum_j c_j\omega_j=0$, reciprocity gives, for every pure $\sigma$,
+
+$$
+\left(\sum_j c_j e_{\omega_j}\right)(\sigma)
+=e_\sigma\left(\sum_j c_j\omega_j\right)=0.
+$$
+
+A functional vanishing on the spanning pure states vanishes everywhere. Thus $\Phi(\sum_jc_j\omega_j)=\sum_jc_je_{\omega_j}$ is well defined and linear. Reciprocity makes $\beta$ symmetric. On any frame decomposition (26.2) gives $\beta(x,x)=\sum_i\lambda_i^2$, which is strictly positive for $x\ne0$. Hence $\Phi$ is injective and, by equal finite dimensions, surjective; its extension is unique.
+
+For $x\in A_+$, (26.2) gives $\lambda_i=e_{\omega_i}(x)\ge0$ in any frame decomposition. Conversely nonnegative frame coefficients give an element of $A_+$. Thus if $x,y\ge0$, writing $x=\sum_i\lambda_i\omega_i$ shows $\beta(x,y)=\sum_i\lambda_i e_{\omega_i}(y)\ge0$. If $\beta(x,y)\ge0$ for all $y\ge0$, its values on the members of a frame for $x$ force every $\lambda_i\ge0$, proving (26.3).
+
+The positive and negative coefficient sums give $\|x\|_B\le\sum_i|\lambda_i|$. Put $h=\sum_i\operatorname{sgn}(\lambda_i)e_{\omega_i}$, with $\operatorname{sgn}(0)=0$. Equation (26.2) gives $-u\le h\le u$, so every $x=a-b$ with $a,b\ge0$ satisfies $h(x)\le u(a)+u(b)$. Since $h(x)=\sum_i|\lambda_i|$, the reverse bound follows. Set $M=\max_i|\lambda_i|$. The same effect inequality gives $-Mu\le\Phi(x)\le Mu$, while evaluation on $\omega_i$ forces any permissible bound $t$ to satisfy $t\ge|\lambda_i|$. This proves (26.4), including $x=0$. Finally bilinearity gives $\beta(x+y,x+y)+\beta(x-y,x-y)=2\beta(x,x)+2\beta(y,y)$. Substituting the two-frame coefficients $(1,1)$ and $(1,-1)$ in (26.4) gives the three stated pairs of sides. $\square$
+
+**适用边界 26.3。** The parallelogram law is derived for $\|\cdot\|_\beta$ only. It is not an operational axiom for either norm in (26.1). Theorem 26.2 packages state-effect self-duality with the explicit three-norm comparison; self-dualizing geometry has antecedents in Müller–Ududec, [Structure of reversible computation determines the self-duality of quantum theory](https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.3516), using bit symmetry, whereas the hypotheses here are S and signed Sp. No implication between those different premise sets is assumed.

+## 27. 光滑球锥的互易缺陷与多面体最小效应障碍
+
+**定理 27.1（球锥替代模型的精确分界）。** For $n\ge2$, let $C_p=\{(t,y)\in\mathbb R\oplus\mathbb R^n:t\ge\|y\|_p\}$ and $u(t,y)=t$. For $1<p<\infty$ put $q=p/(p-1)$. Every pure state is $\omega_x=(1,x)$ with $\|x\|_p=1$. Its complete saturating-effect set and its least member are
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+f_s(t,y)&=(1-s)t+s\langle x^\sharp,y\rangle,\quad 0\le s\le\tfrac12,
+&x^\sharp_i&=\operatorname{sgn}(x_i)|x_i|^{p-1},\\
+e_x(t,y)&=\tfrac12\bigl(t+\langle x^\sharp,y\rangle\bigr).
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{27.1}
+$$
+
+At $x=e_1$ and $y=2^{-1/p}(e_1+e_2)$, the reciprocity defect is
+
+$$
+\left|e_x(\omega_y)-e_y(\omega_x)\right|
+=\frac12\left|2^{-1/p}-2^{1/p-1}\right|,
+\tag{27.2}
+$$
+
+which vanishes exactly at $p=2$. Both endpoint cones $C_1,C_\infty$ have no least saturating effect at any vertex pure state. By contrast, for every integer $N\ge1$, the classical cone $\mathbb R_+^N$ with $u(x)=\sum_i x_i$ satisfies S and Sp. Thus within these alternatives the smooth ball cones meet S exactly at $p=2$, while classical simplices remain admitted.

+**证明。** Strict convexity of the $p$ ball identifies all its boundary points as its extreme points. Hölder duality says that $f(t,y)=\alpha t+\langle g,y\rangle$ is an effect exactly when

+$$
+\|g\|_q\le\alpha,\qquad \|g\|_q\le1-\alpha.
+$$

+Saturation gives $1-\alpha=\langle g,x\rangle\le\|g\|_q\le1-\alpha$. Equality in Hölder for $1<p<\infty$ forces $g=sx^\sharp$, where $s=1-\alpha=\|g\|_q$, and the other inequality gives $0\le s\le1/2$. This also covers $g=0$. Conversely every effect in (27.1) saturates. Moreover
+
+$$
+f_s-e_x=(\tfrac12-s)\bigl(t-\langle x^\sharp,y\rangle\bigr)\ge0
+\quad\text{on }C_p,
+$$
+
+so $e_x$ is the least member. The two evaluations in (27.2) are $(1+2^{-1/p})/2$ and $(1+2^{1/p-1})/2$. Equality of their nonconstant terms is equivalent to $-1/p=1/p-1$, hence to $p=2$. At $p=2$, (27.1) is reciprocal for every pair. In fact every $C_p$ with $1<p<\infty$ satisfies Sp: if $z\ne0$, put $v=z/\|z\|_p$ and write
+
+$$

+$$

+The two states are distinguished by $e_v,e_{-v}$, whose sum is $u$; for $z=0$ choose any unit $v$. Thus failure of reciprocity is isolated even among these signed-spectral models.

+For $p=\infty$, take vertices $a=(1,1,1,1,\ldots,1)$, $b=(1,1,-1,1,\ldots,1)$, $c=(1,-1,1,1,\ldots,1)$, $d=(1,-1,-1,1,\ldots,1)$. The effects $h_1=(t+y_1)/2$ and $h_2=(t+y_2)/2$ saturate $a$. A least saturating effect $h$ would obey $0\le h\le h_1,h_2$, so $h(b)=h(c)=0$ and $h(a)=1$. But $a+d=b+c$ forces $h(d)=-1$, contradicting positivity. Their convex combinations give the saturating family $h_\theta=(t+\theta y_1+(1-\theta)y_2)/2$, $0\le\theta\le1$. Signed coordinate permutations carry this contradiction to every vertex. The square cross-section at $n=2$ is the local gbit cone, also the marginal cone for PR-box models.

+## 28. Jordan 桥、相干面过滤与多线性干涉边界
+
+**定义 28.1（强对称与完整 compression 合同）。** In Definition 26.1 a reversible map is a linear cone automorphism preserving $u$, with group topology inherited from $\operatorname{GL}(A)$. Strong symmetry means that a group of such maps acts transitively on ordered frames of every fixed size for which frames exist. For a positive idempotent linear map $T:A\to A$, write $\operatorname{im}_+T=\operatorname{im}T\cap A_+$ and $\ker_+T=\ker T\cap A_+$. It is complemented if some positive idempotent $R$ satisfies $\operatorname{im}_+T=\ker_+R$ and $\ker_+T=\operatorname{im}_+R$.
+
+A coherent face filter is a positive idempotent $T$ such that $u(Tx)\le u(x)$ for $x\ge0$, both $T$ and its dual $T^\vee$ are complemented, its positive range is the specified face, and it is neutral: $u(Tx)=u(x)$ with $x\ge0$ implies $Tx=x$. This is the state-side version of an Alfsen–Shultz compression; neutrality follows from their full definition and is displayed here to specify the operational disturbance condition. The distinction between state-side filters and effect-side compressions, including both complement conditions, is given in Barnum–Müller–Ududec, [Higher-order interference and single-system postulates characterizing quantum theory](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.4147), Definitions 13–14, using Alfsen–Shultz, Geometry of State Spaces of Operator Algebras (2003), Definition 7.22.
+
+Operationally choose disjoint blocks $B_i$ of a frame, set $a_i=\sum_{j\in B_i}e_{\omega_j}$, and define $F_i=\{x\ge0:a_i(x)=u(x)\}$. For a slit set $S$, let $F_S$ be the smallest face containing all $F_i$, $i\in S$, with $F_\varnothing=\{0\}$. A coherent slit family uses the coherent face filter onto $F_S$ for each $S$. This is a restriction on the operations used in the slit experiment, not a claim about every positive instrument.
+
+**定理 28.2（操作最小效应至二次 slit 响应的条件桥与反例判据）。** Suppose S, Sp and strong symmetry hold in Definition 26.1, and slit operations satisfy Definition 28.1. Then $A$ is order-isomorphic, preserving $u$, to a Euclidean Jordan algebra $J$ with its cone of squares and Jordan trace $\tau$; it is either simple or a classical algebra $\mathbb R^N$. In this representation $\beta(x,y)=\tau(x\circ y)$. For any orthogonal idempotents $p_1,\ldots,p_k$ in $J$, any state $\omega$, and any effect $e$, the coherent response is
+
+$$
+f(S)=e(Q(p_S)\omega),\quad p_S=\sum_{i\in S}p_i,\quad
+Q(a)=2L_a^2-L_{a\circ a},\quad L_a b=a\circ b.
+\tag{28.1}
+$$
+
+With $Q(a,b)=L_aL_b+L_bL_a-L_{a\circ b}$ and indicators $s_i=\mathbf1_{i\in S}$, its unique multilinear polynomial is
+
+$$
+f(S)=\sum_i e(Q(p_i)\omega)s_i
++2\sum_{i<j}e(Q(p_i,p_j)\omega)s_is_j.
+\tag{28.2}
+$$
+
+Consequently, for disjoint sets $B,T$ with $|T|\ge3$,
+
+$$
+I_T(B)=\sum_{R\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T|-|R|}f(B\cup R)=0.
+\tag{28.3}
+$$
+
+These identities hold in every Euclidean Jordan algebra, including the Albert algebra. Every simple such algebra of rank at least two has a state, effect and two slits with $I_{\{1,2\}}(\varnothing)=1/2$; the complex qubit realizes this value with $\omega=E=|+\rangle\langle+|$ and coordinate slits. Classical associative algebras have $I_{\{i,j\}}(B)=0$ identically. A response having any nonzero multilinear coefficient of degree at least three cannot be a coherent-compression response of such a system.

+**证明。** First match the hypotheses of the attributed intermediate classification [Barnum–Hilgert, Strongly symmetric spectral convex bodies are Jordan algebra state spaces, Theorem 1.1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.03753). This is the specialization of Gregoratti–Werner, [*Quantum Lost and Found*, Proposition 8, equations (18)–(21)](https://arxiv.org/html/quant-ph/0209025v1#ThmThe8), with input and output dimension four and the fixed two-operator decomposition furnished by (6.7). +The rank-two correlation example in Buscemi–Chiribella–D’Ariano, [*Inverting Quantum Decoherence by Classical Feedback from the Environment*, equation (9)](https://arxiv.org/html/quant-ph/0504195v5), is the entrywise conjugate of $C_0$, with the Heisenberg/Schrödinger correspondence specified in Section 4.
